steps.tx: Extra-adrenal neuroendocrine tumours arising from sympathetic or parasympathetic autonomic ganglia represent the developmental counterparts of intra-adrenal phaeochromocytomas. Designated as a **paraganglioma**, these tumours originate along the sympathetic chain in the abdomen, retroperitoneum, and thorax, or parasympathetic ganglia in the skull base and neck. Sympathetic paragangliomas, frequently located at the aortic bifurcation (organ of Zuckerkandl), synthesize norepinephrine and present with catecholamine hypersecretion, severe hypertension, and tachycardia. Parasympathetic paragangliomas (such as carotid body tumours, glomus jugulare, and glomus vagale) are predominantly non-secretory, presenting as painless neck masses or pulsatile tinnitus.
steps.say: Extra-adrenal neuroendocrine tumours arising from autonomic ganglia represent the counterparts of adrenal phaeochromocytomas. Designated as a paraganglioma, these tumours originate along the sympathetic chain in the abdomen, or parasympathetic ganglia in the skull base. Sympathetic paragangliomas, often located at the organ of Zuckerkandl, synthesize norepinephrine and present with catecholamine hypersecretion. Parasympathetic tumours like carotid body tumours are predominantly non-secretory, presenting as neck masses or pulsatile tinnitus.

steps.tx: Historically taught epidemiological proportions provided a classic framework for understanding chromaffin cell tumour behaviour and distribution. The traditional clinical **rule of 10** stated that roughly ten percent of phaeochromocytomas are extra-adrenal (paragangliomas), ten percent are bilateral, ten percent are malignant, and ten percent are familial. However, modern genomic sequencing has substantially revised these figures, demonstrating that upwards of thirty-five to forty percent of all phaeochromocytomas harbour identifiable germline mutations. In extra-adrenal abdominal paragangliomas, the rate of malignancy is far higher, approaching fifty percent in patients harbouring SDHB mutations.

In extra-adrenal paragangliomas, malignancy rates approach fifty percent in patients with succinate dehydrogenase B mutations.

steps.tx: An autosomal dominant multisystem tumour predisposition syndrome features bilateral phaeochromocytomas driven by pseudohypoxic signaling. Caused by inactivating germline mutations in the VHL tumour suppressor gene on chromosome 3p25, **von hippel-lindau** disease leads to stabilization of hypoxia-inducible factors under normoxic conditions. Phaeochromocytomas develop in ten to twenty percent of VHL patients, characteristically presenting at a young age, often bilateral, and predominantly secreting norepinephrine. Associated lesions include retinal and cerebellar hemangioblastomas, clear cell renal cell carcinomas, multiple pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours and benign cysts, and endolymphatic sac tumours.

steps.tx: A common neurocutaneous phacomatosis caused by autosomal dominant mutations in the NF1 tumour suppressor gene on chromosome 17q11 confers increased chromaffin neoplasia risk. Diagnosing **neurofibromatosis type 1** (von Recklinghausen disease) relies on physical hallmarks: six or more café-au-lait macules, axillary freckling (Crowe sign), multiple cutaneous neurofibromas, Lisch nodules, and optic pathway gliomas. Phaeochromocytomas develop in one to five percent of NF1 patients, rising significantly in NF1 patients presenting with refractory hypertension, mandating biochemical catecholamine screening before initiating standard antihypertensive therapy.

steps.tx: Mitochondrial enzyme complex mutations orchestrate hereditary paraganglioma-phaeochromocytoma syndromes with distinct clinical behaviours and inheritance patterns. Inactivating germline mutations in succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) subunit genes cause intracellular succinate accumulation, inhibiting prolyl hydroxylases and creating pseudohypoxia. Mutations in **sdhb** confer a strikingly high risk of aggressive extra-adrenal malignancy exceeding forty percent. Conversely, SDHD mutations exhibit maternal genomic imprinting; disease manifests only when the mutated allele is inherited from the father, characteristically producing multiple benign head and neck parasympathetic paragangliomas.

steps.tx: Functional molecular imaging is vital for whole-body staging of paragangliomas, outperforming standard computed tomography in detecting multicentric and metastatic disease. Positron emission tomography using fluorine-18-fluorodeoxyglucose (**fdg-pet**) or gallium-68-DOTATATE PET/CT demonstrates exceptional sensitivity for SDH-mutated extra-adrenal tumours and metastases. Gallium-68-DOTATATE binds somatostatin receptor subtype two (SSTR2) overexpressed on paraganglioma cells, achieving detection rates exceeding ninety-five percent. This imaging modality successfully identifies occult osseous and lymph node metastases, mapping the extent of disease and guiding targeted peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with lutetium-177 in inoperable malignant cases.

steps.tx: Preoperative medical optimization for secretory paragangliomas adheres strictly to the adrenergic blockade principles established for intra-adrenal phaeochromocytomas. Administering oral **alpha-blockade** with phenoxybenzamine or doxazosin for at least ten to fourteen days expands intravascular volume and blunts catecholamine-induced vasoconstriction. Beta-blockers are co-administered only after therapeutic alpha-blockade is verified. Intraoperatively, extensive retroperitoneal resection requires careful preservation of adjacent major vessels, accompanied by continuous invasive arterial line blood pressure monitoring and immediate availability of intravenous nitroprusside and norepinephrine.

steps.tx: Universal germline genetic testing is now formally mandated for every patient diagnosed with a phaeochromocytoma or paraganglioma, regardless of age or family history. Demonstrating a specific **germline mutation** identifies syndromic associations, guides lifelong multiorgan screening, and enables cascade genetic predictive testing in asymptomatic first-degree relatives. Identifying mutations in SDHB mandates aggressive lifelong oncological surveillance due to high metastatic potential, ensuring that multicentric neuroendocrine tumours are excised before incurable metastatic dissemination occurs.
